title: A test must not scroll the page itself before it asserts the element is in the viewport
rule: When a test proves that the app brings an element into view (`toBeInViewport`, a position check), do not call `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` or `hover` on that element first: both scroll the page and make the assertion unable to fail. If the assertion fails after a layout change, fix the app. Moving a part from a pane to a longer page often means the app must now scroll the page as well as its inner scroller.
rationale: E41.5 (#451): the glyph-search spec, moved to the family page, gained a `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` before `toBeInViewport`, which hid that the searched glyph landed below the window at 1280x800.
